The answer is **3.95**, taken as the regression-adjusted estimate of the treatment effect.

I regressed the outcome `y` on the treatment indicator and all 25 covariates (x1–x25) by OLS. The coefficient on `treatment` is 3.947 (SE 0.135). The dataset has 747 units, 139 of them treated.

Other estimators give different values, so the answer depends on the method:

| Method | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Naive difference in means | 3.66 |
| OLS, treatment + covariates (chosen) | 3.95 |
| T-learner (separate outcome regressions) | 3.68 |
| AIPW (doubly robust) | 3.70 |
| IPW | 3.34 |

The question doesn't name an estimator, so I took the most standard covariate-adjusted reading. If it expects AIPW or another method, the answer changes accordingly.

ANSWER: 3.95
